title: Boolean Algebra & K-Maps
summary: Boolean Algebra is the mathematical framework for analyzing and simplifying digital logic circuits. Karnaugh Maps (K-Maps) provide a visual method for minimizing Boolean expressions into Sum-Of-Products (SOP).

working_principle: Boolean expressions are simplified using fundamental algebraic laws (Identity, Null, Idempotent, Complement, DeMorgan's). K-Maps group adjacent 1s into powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8) to eliminate redundant variables.
boolean_equation: DeMorgan: (A · B)' = A' + B',  (A + B)' = A' · B'
applications: Gate Minimization in FPGA and ASIC Design
Reducing Total IC Package Count on Printed Circuit Boards
Optimizing ALU Execution Speed by Reducing Propagation Delay
advantages: Reduces gate count and manufacturing cost
Decreases circuit power consumption and thermal dissipation
disadvantages: K-Maps become difficult for expressions exceeding 5-6 variables (Requires Quine-McCluskey algorithm)
common_mistakes: Grouping K-Map cells in non-power-of-2 sizes (e.g. grouping 3 or 5 cells).
Forgetting Gray Code cell ordering on K-Map headers (00, 01, 11, 10).
quick_notes: K-Map cells follow Gray code order.
DeMorgan's Theorem converts AND-OR to NAND-NAND.

viva_questions.a: 1) The complement of a product is equal to the sum of the complements: (A·B)' = A'+B'. 2) The complement of a sum is equal to the product of the complements: (A+B)' = A'·B'.
SOP = Sum Of Products (AND terms ORed together). POS = Product Of Sums (OR terms ANDed together).

interview_questions.q: Why must K-Map adjacent cells use Gray Code sequence?
interview_questions.a: Because Gray Code ensures only 1 variable changes state between adjacent cells, allowing algebraic factoring out of that variable.
